Why was Okonkwo famous?
questions.comprehension_passage: Read the passage and answer the given subquestions. Okonkwo was well known throughout the nine villages and even beyond. His fame rested on solid personal achievements. As a young man of eighteen, he had brought honour to his village by throwing Amalinze the Cat. Amalinze was the great wrestler who, for seven years, was unbeaten, from Umuofia to Mbaino. He was called the Cat because his back would never touch the earth. It was this man that Okonkwo threw in a fight, which the old men agreed was one of the fiercest since the founder of their town engaged a spirit of the wild for seven days and seven nights. The drums beat, and the flutes sang, and the spectators held their breath. Amalinze was a wily craftsman, but Okonkwo was as slippery as a fish in water. Every nerve and every muscle stood out on their arms, on their backs and their thighs, and one almost heard them stretching to breaking point. In the end, Okonkwo threw the Cat. That was many years ago, twenty years or more, and during this time, Okonkwo's fame had grown like a bushfire in the harmattan. He was tall and huge, and his bushy eyebrows and wide nose gave him a very severe look. He breathed heavily, and it was said that, when he slept, his wives and children in their houses could hear him breathe. When he walked, his heels hardly touched the ground, and he seemed to walk on springs, as if he was going to pounce on somebody. And he did pounce on people quite often. He had a slight stammer, and whenever he was angry and could not get his words out quickly enough, he would use his fists. He had no patience with unsuccessful men. He had had no patience with his father. Unoka, for that was his father's name, had died ten years ago. In his day, he was lazy and improvident and was quite incapable of thinking about tomorrow. If any money came his way, and it seldom did, he immediately bought gourds of palm-wine, called round his neighbours and made merry. He always said that whenever he saw a dead man's mouth, he saw the folly of not eating what one had in one's lifetime. Unoka was, of course, a debtor, and he owed every neighbour some money, from a few cowries to quite substantial amounts. Source: Things Fall Apart – Chinua Achebe

questions.comprehension_passage: Go through this passage and answer the given subquestions: Ready to fill out the JLF 2025 Volunteer Application Form? Just give us a few minutes of your time. Before you embark on your journey to volunteer at the Jaipur Literature Festival, we have some crucial insights to share . We know your eagerness to participate is unmatched, but even the most dedicated individuals can make inadvertent errors that might impact their chances. In a sea of thousands of applications, we're invested in making your application count. Allow us to provide you with a guide to make it through with flying colours. The diligence with which you approach this application speaks volumes about your dedication. It reflects your attention to detail and your commitment—qualities that we hold in high regard among our volunteers. Before you proceed pause to reflect. Assess your strengths and expectations carefully. While our application window extends till 10th November 2024, waiting until the eleventh hour isn't advised. Remember, applications are evaluated on a 'first come, first serve' basis. Who Are We Seeking to Join Us? We're on the lookout for enthusiastic college students and working professionals who yearn to explore the inner workings of the Jaipur Literature Festival and get hands-on management experience. It's an opportunity to witness first-hand what goes into orchestrating an event of this magnitude. Essential Insights for a Successful Application: Genuine Responses Matter: We urge you to express your unique reasons for wanting to volunteer. A simple copy-paste of generic 'reasons to volunteer' won't set you apart. Refrain from using Quora, Google, Chat-GPT/Bard etc. The questions asked are deeply personal and we want to know the person you are! Professional Tone: As this is a foray into a professional realm, formal language is essential. Avoid using abbreviations, SMS lingo, or emoticons. Birthdate Accuracy: If you're under 18, we regret that you're ineligible. Ensure that your birthdate is accurately recorded; errors can lead to confusion. Email Professionalism: Select an email ID that conveys professionalism; our official correspondence will be via email. Correct Contact Information: Provide reliable contact details as they will be used for communication. Precision matters here. Concise Expression: When addressing the statement of purpose, be succinct while conveying your intent clearly. We receive a substantial volume of applications, and brevity helps us maintain fairness. Language Preference: This year, you can fill out the form in English and Hindi. Please choose the language you are comfortable with, allowing you to express your ideas clearly. Remember, the Festival requires volunteers who are comfortable with at least one or both of these languages. Source: https://jaipurliteraturefestival.org/volunteer
